title: Olaparib after first-line ovarian cancer treatment
context_label: BRCA1/2-mutated advanced ovarian, fallopian-tube or primary-peritoneal cancer after first-line platinum response
indication_text: Maintenance for adults with FIGO III–IV, BRCA1/2-mutated high-grade epithelial ovarian, fallopian-tube or primary-peritoneal cancer in complete or partial response after first-line platinum chemotherapy.
purpose: Help keep the cancer controlled after the first platinum chemotherapy has reduced it or made it undetectable, in a cancer with a qualifying BRCA1 or BRCA2 change.
schedule_label: Olaparib tablets morning and evening, every day
schedule_summary: Take your prescribed olaparib dose morning and evening every day, without a planned rest week. Olaparib continues until cancer progression or unacceptable side effects, with a planned two-year decision. If scans show no disease after two years, treatment is completed. If disease remains, the consultant may consider continuing when further benefit is expected.
administration_text: The usual starting dose is 300 mg of olaparib tablets twice daily, with or without food. Olaparib continues until cancer progression or unacceptable side effects, with a planned two-year decision. If scans show no disease after two years, treatment is completed. If disease remains, the consultant may consider continuing when further benefit is expected. Follow your own prescription if the dose changes.
monitoring_summary: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests every four weeks for the first 12 months, then as clinically indicated. Review symptoms, food/fluid intake, medicines and tablet supply; abnormal results or new symptoms can require earlier checks.

safety_note: Follow your own prescription and hospital contact plan. Dose changes and treatment restarts are decisions for your treating team.
urgent_extra: Call your oncology team urgently for fever, shaking chills, feeling suddenly unwell, unusual bruising or bleeding, marked weakness, new or worsening cough or breathlessness, a new painful swollen limb, yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, or inability to keep fluids down. Follow your own temperature and contact plan; do not wait for the next appointment. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, seizures or stroke symptoms: call 112/999.

consent_support: Discuss the expected disease-control benefit, trial uncertainty, alternatives and your priorities. Review common effects and serious marrow, lung, clotting, liver and allergic risks. Olaparib can harm an unborn baby. Discuss fertility and pregnancy prevention before treatment. If you could become pregnant, use two reliable complementary contraception methods during treatment and for six months after the last dose, following your team’s advice. A non-hormonal method may be needed because olaparib can reduce the effect of some hormonal contraceptives; hormone-sensitive cancer also affects the choice. Pregnancy testing is needed before treatment and may be repeated. Do not breastfeed during olaparib or for one month after the last dose. Tell the team immediately if pregnancy is possible.

agents.name: Olaparib
agents.mechanism: Olaparib is a PARP inhibitor: it blocks proteins that help repair damaged DNA and can trap them on the DNA. Cancer cells with a harmful BRCA1 or BRCA2 change already have difficulty using an important repair pathway. Blocking PARP can leave more damage than these cells can repair. Normal blood-forming cells can also be affected, which explains why blood counts and symptom checks remain important during targeted treatment.

risks: Anaemia, sometimes requiring transfusion; low white cells or platelets with infection or bleeding risk
Nausea, vomiting, indigestion, diarrhoea, reduced appetite and changes in taste
Fatigue or weakness, headache, dizziness and mouth soreness
Serious persistent blood-count changes, including MDS/AML; the risk varies with the treatment setting and previous therapy
Pneumonitis: inflammation of the lungs that can be serious or fatal
Blood clots in veins or lungs; symptoms need urgent assessment
Liver injury and changes in kidney blood tests; the team may need to review treatment
Allergic reactions and harm to an unborn baby; discuss fertility, contraception and breastfeeding where relevant
agents.watch: Agree a written anti-sickness plan with your team, including what is prescribed regularly, what is for rescue, and when to call if it is not working. NCCP classifies oral olaparib as moderate-to-high sickness risk, but a fixed intravenous chemotherapy anti-sickness cycle does not apply. Some people need prescribed support and others do not need routine prevention. A stomach-acid medicine may be considered for symptoms under local policy.
visual: DNA damage accumulates in susceptible cells

anatomy: Fatigue, headache or dizziness can affect daily life. Marked tiredness, pallor, breathlessness or a fast heartbeat can also signal anaemia; report a change rather than assuming it is expected.
Taste changes, soreness and poor appetite may make eating difficult. Ask early for symptom and nutrition support.
New cough or breathlessness needs prompt assessment for infection, lung inflammation or a clot. Severe breathing difficulty or chest pain needs emergency help.

Blood tests check liver and kidney function and help the team review the dose. Report yellow skin or eyes, dark urine or right-sided upper abdominal pain. A changed creatinine result needs interpretation, not a self-directed dose change.
Take prescribed sickness support. Call if vomiting or diarrhoea persists, you cannot drink, or pain is severe.

Low red cells can cause tiredness or breathlessness; low white cells can increase infection risk; low platelets can cause bruising or bleeding. Persistent unexplained changes may need specialist marrow tests.
Report unusual bruising, bleeding, fever, shivers or suddenly feeling unwell. Do not wait for the next blood test.
A new painful swollen leg needs urgent assessment. Sudden chest pain or severe breathlessness is an emergency.

phases.label: Daily olaparib tablets
phases.detail: Olaparib continues until cancer progression or unacceptable side effects, with a planned two-year decision. If scans show no disease after two years, treatment is completed. If disease remains, the consultant may consider continuing when further benefit is expected.

timeline.label: Daily prescribed olaparib
timeline.text: Swallow the prescribed tablets whole with or without food, once in the morning and once in the evening. Do not chew, crush, dissolve or divide them. The usual starting dose is two 150 mg tablets each time (300 mg twice daily); your own dose may be lower. Check both tablet strength and tablet count after every prescription change. If you miss a dose, take the next normal dose at its usual time; do not double up. Do not substitute olaparib capsules for tablets. Avoid grapefruit juice and check other grapefruit or bitter-orange products with your pharmacist.

support.title: Your prescribed sickness plan
support.text: Agree a written anti-sickness plan with your team, including what is prescribed regularly, what is for rescue, and when to call if it is not working. NCCP classifies oral olaparib as moderate-to-high sickness risk, but a fixed intravenous chemotherapy anti-sickness cycle does not apply. Some people need prescribed support and others do not need routine prevention. A stomach-acid medicine may be considered for symptoms under local policy.

support.title: Check every new medicine
support.text: Give the pharmacist a complete list of prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins and herbal products. Some antibiotics, antifungals, seizure medicines and St John’s wort can change how much olaparib reaches your body. Even anti-sickness treatment needs checking: aprepitant can increase olaparib exposure. Do not start a borrowed support medicine, change the olaparib dose or restart a paused course yourself.

support.title: Blood counts and extra support
support.text: Blood counts check red cells that carry oxygen, white cells that help fight infection and platelets that help stop bleeding. Low counts can lead to a pause, a lower prescribed dose, a transfusion or further tests. Persistent or unexplained changes sometimes need specialist bone-marrow tests to investigate myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukaemia (MDS/AML). These are serious conditions; their risk differs by treatment setting and previous therapy. A treatment pause is not itself a diagnosis. There is no automatic white-cell injection, antibiotic or steroid course for everyone.

support.title: Eating, drinking and daily life
support.text: Ask for help early if nausea, mouth soreness, taste changes or poor appetite affect eating. Keep the team informed about weight loss or difficulty drinking. Fatigue may need a dose or blood-count review. Do not drive or use machinery if dizzy, weak or very tired.

support.title: A treatment pause
support.text: A prescribed pause can give blood counts or symptoms time to improve. It does not mean treatment has failed. Keep the agreed tests and ask exactly when the team will review restarting. Never take catch-up tablets.

support.title: Support for your wider treatment
support.text: Keep postoperative, nutrition, pain and symptom-support plans that still apply. Ask early about ongoing abdominal symptoms, appetite, fatigue, menopausal effects, sexual health or emotional support. Other treatment and symptom medicines keep their own prescribed schedules.

support.title: Fertility, contraception and breastfeeding

sections.title: Before the first dose

sections.title: How maintenance fits after chemotherapy
sections.text: The first platinum course controls the cancer; maintenance aims to sustain that control. NCCP ordinarily starts olaparib within eight weeks of the last platinum dose, with a twelve-week allowance where debulking surgery is required. Your team confirms timing. If bevacizumab was started with chemotherapy, any switch to olaparib alone is a separate agreed plan.

Avoid grapefruit juice and check other grapefruit or bitter-orange products with your pharmacist. Keep enough supply for weekends, holidays and the next review. Olaparib itself needs no infusion pump or port.

sections.title: If treatment is paused
sections.text: Ask why it is paused, which tests are next and when the team will contact you. Only the prescriber can confirm the restart dose. Do not take catch-up tablets.

sections.title: Reviewing benefit and the next step
sections.text: Olaparib continues until cancer progression or unacceptable side effects, with a planned two-year decision. If scans show no disease after two years, treatment is completed. If disease remains, the consultant may consider continuing when further benefit is expected. The consultant sets symptom review, scans and any CA-125 monitoring. CA-125 is a blood marker used in some ovarian cancers; it is interpreted with symptoms and imaging. Agree the two-year scan/review decision separately from the four-week safety tests.

sections.title: Genetic results and family questions
sections.text: BRCA1 and BRCA2 help repair damaged DNA. A germline change is present in the body’s cells and may have implications for relatives. A tumour-only change does not by itself show that it is inherited. Ask which test you had, what the result means and whether genetic counselling is appropriate. A variant of uncertain significance is not automatically a treatment-qualifying result.

sections.title: Before leaving the clinic
sections.text: Confirm the next tests, review, tablet supply and verified daytime/out-of-hours contact numbers. Ask what to do if a result or prescription has not arrived.

items.text: New or worsening cough, breathlessness, chest pain or a painful swollen limb can signal infection, lung inflammation or a clot. Do not assume these symptoms are routine fatigue.

items.title: Liver and blood changes
items.text: Yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, unexplained severe fatigue, infections, bruising or bleeding need prompt advice. Persistent symptoms still matter during a treatment break or after treatment ends.

chapters.title: Evidence and your choices
chapters.intro: Trial results describe groups and should support a discussion about your priorities.

items.title: SOLO1: maintenance after the first platinum response
items.text: In the original analysis, the estimated proportion alive without cancer progression at three years was 60% with olaparib and 27% with placebo. This supports maintenance treatment after a response. The figure is a trial-group estimate, not an individual forecast or a three-year tablet course.

items.title: What the comparison cannot tell us
items.text: The study population was specifically selected for BRCA-mutated first-line disease. Results are not a direct comparison with olaparib plus bevacizumab and should not be transferred to relapsed disease.

items.title: Your priorities
items.text: Ask about expected benefit, side effects, alternatives including symptom-focused care, and choosing to decline or stop treatment. Decisions can be revisited as your health or priorities change.

evidence.title: SOLO1: maintenance after the first platinum response
evidence.intro: SOLO1 compared olaparib with placebo in 391 people with newly diagnosed advanced BRCA-mutated ovarian, fallopian-tube or primary-peritoneal cancer responding to platinum. The main published 2018 endpoint was time without progression or death.
evidence.population: BRCA-mutated advanced disease after a first-line platinum response

A variant of uncertain significance is not automatically a treatment-qualifying result.

questions.q: What should I know before taking support medicines?
questions.a: Agree a written anti-sickness plan with your team, including what is prescribed regularly, what is for rescue, and when to call if it is not working. NCCP classifies oral olaparib as moderate-to-high sickness risk, but a fixed intravenous chemotherapy anti-sickness cycle does not apply. Some people need prescribed support and others do not need routine prevention. A stomach-acid medicine may be considered for symptoms under local policy. Give the pharmacist a complete list of prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins and herbal products. Some antibiotics, antifungals, seizure medicines and St John’s wort can change how much olaparib reaches your body. Even anti-sickness treatment needs checking: aprepitant can increase olaparib exposure. Do not start a borrowed support medicine, change the olaparib dose or restart a paused course yourself.

patient_summary.purpose: Help keep the cancer controlled after the first platinum chemotherapy has reduced it or made it undetectable, in a cancer with a qualifying BRCA1 or BRCA2 change.
patient_summary.schedule: Olaparib tablets morning and evening, every day

phases.title: Daily tablets
phases.text: The usual starting dose is 300 mg of olaparib tablets twice daily, with or without food. Olaparib continues until cancer progression or unacceptable side effects, with a planned two-year decision. If scans show no disease after two years, treatment is completed. If disease remains, the consultant may consider continuing when further benefit is expected. Follow your own prescription if the dose changes.

monitoring.when: Confirm the BRCA1/2 result, cancer type/stage, response to first-line platinum, surgery/recovery and start date. Check full blood count, kidney/liver profile, medicines and pregnancy testing where relevant.

monitoring.test: Safety blood tests and symptom review
monitoring.when: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests every four weeks for the first 12 months, then as clinically indicated. Review symptoms, food/fluid intake, medicines and tablet supply; abnormal results or new symptoms can require earlier checks.

The consultant sets symptom review, scans and any CA-125 monitoring. CA-125 is a blood marker used in some ovarian cancers; it is interpreted with symptoms and imaging. Agree the two-year scan/review decision separately from the four-week safety tests.

cycle_expectations: Symptoms may occur on any day; there is no planned rest week. Report new problems promptly.
Use only your prescribed sickness/rescue medicines. Call if vomiting, diarrhoea or poor intake persists; do not wait for the next review.
preparation: Confirm the BRCA1/2 result, cancer type/stage, response to first-line platinum, surgery/recovery and start date. Check full blood count, kidney/liver profile, medicines and pregnancy testing where relevant.
Confirm tablet strength, supply, written support instructions and verified daytime/out-of-hours contact numbers.
patient_summary.card_schedule: Tablets twice daily; planned two-year disease-status review.
patient_summary.card_record_note: Recording spaces do not define the planned course.
patient_summary.card_alert: Fever, suddenly unwell, unusual bleeding or new breathlessness: contact the team urgently. Severe symptoms: 112/999.

cycle_blocks.label: Every day
cycle_blocks.text: Morning and evening tablets at the prescribed dose; no planned rest week.

cycle_blocks.label: Between reviews
cycle_blocks.text: Keep the support plan and report symptoms promptly.

cycle_blocks.label: Next review
cycle_blocks.text: Check blood results, symptoms, supply and the next prescribed dose.
